step1_analysis.description: A behavioral model of a Q-enhanced LC bandpass filter. It uses an input transconductance (gmi) to inject current into an RLC tank, and a negative transconductance (gmn, typically implemented as a cross-coupled pair) to compensate for the tank's parasitic losses, thereby enhancing the quality factor (Q) and narrowing the bandwidth.

paper_reference.title: A 2.5-GHz Low-Power, High Dynamic Range, Self-Tuned Q-Enhanced LC Filter in SOI

center_frequency.description: The resonant frequency of the LC tank where the filter exhibits maximum gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by L and C values: f0 = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). For L=1nH and C=4.053pF, f0 = 2.5 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The center frequency is set by the passive components and is independent of the technology node in this behavioral model.

voltage_gain.description: The peak voltage gain at the center frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = gmi * Reff, where Reff is the effective parallel resistance of the tank after Q-enhancement. With gmi=25.17mS and Reff=562 ohms, Gain = 14.14 V/V = 23 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Targeting the paper's specification by setting the behavioral transconductance parameters appropriately.

sky130_expected.calculation: BW = f0 / Qeff, where Qeff = Reff / (w0 * L).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Targeting the paper's specification by tuning the negative transconductance (gmn) to achieve the desired Qeff.

q_factor.description: The effective quality factor of the filter.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Derived directly from the center frequency and bandwidth requirements.

step3_testbench.description: AC analysis to measure the center frequency, peak voltage gain, 3-dB bandwidth, and Q-factor of the behavioral Q-enhanced LC filter.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Q-Enhanced LC Filter Testbench

* Behavioral parameters to match paper specs (2.5GHz, 70MHz BW, 23dB Gain)
.param Rs_val=50
.param Rp_val=157
.param C_val=4.053p
.param L_val=1n
.param gmi_val=25.17m
.param gmn_val=-4.59m

* Original pseudo-SPICE netlist from paper:
* V1 Vs GND AC
* Rs Vs Vi Rs
* gmi (Vi GND N1 GND) amplifier
* Rp N1 GND Rp
* C N1 GND
* L N1 GND
* gmn (N1 GND N1 GND) amplifier

* Adapted valid ngspice netlist:
V1 Vs GND dc 0 ac 1
Rs Vs Vi {Rs_val}
Gmi N1 GND Vi GND {gmi_val}
Rp N1 GND {Rp_val}
C N1 GND {C_val}
L N1 GND {L_val}
Gmn N1 GND N1 GND {gmn_val}

.control
* High resolution AC sweep around the 2.5 GHz center frequency
ac lin 2000 2G 3G

* Calculate voltage gain in dB (from filter input Vi to output N1)
let gain_db = vdb(N1) - vdb(Vi)

* Measure peak gain
meas ac max_gain max gain_db

* Calculate 3-dB drop level
let gain_3db = max_gain - 3

* Measure lower and upper 3-dB frequencies
meas ac f_low when gain_db=gain_3db rise=1
meas ac f_high when gain_db=gain_3db fall=1

* Calculate Bandwidth, Center Frequency, and Q-factor
let bw = f_high - f_low
let f_center = (f_low + f_high) / 2
let q_factor = f_center / bw

* Print results
print max_gain f_center bw q_factor
quit
.endc
.end
